title: Render each bee agent from its role instead of its cost tier
action: Slice 2. Onboarding renders each agent file with a model chosen from the tier tables: AGENT_TIER_BY_NAME (onboard/templates.rs:222-230) maps agent to tier, AGENT_TIER_DEFAULTS_CLAUDE and the opencode twin (:234-249) map tier to a default model, and agents.rs:129-147 substitutes {{TIER_MODEL}} from the slot map. Rebase that chain onto ROLE: an agent declares the role it serves, and its rendered model comes from resolving that role through the shared resolver of mrs-2, so a host that configures a role gets it in the rendered agent file with no second code path. SCOPE FENCE: this cell changes the MECHANISM only. Which role names bee publishes as shipped config defaults is decision D3 (store 3c9d6262) and belongs to the cell that adds the cell role field — do not invent or publish a default name list here. If the rebase forces a naming choice you cannot make without D3, return BLOCKED with the proposal rather than guessing. Onboarding writes files a host depends on, so a rendered file that changes shape must be named on the cap with what a host sees differently.

truths: An agent's rendered model comes from resolving its declared role through the one shared resolver, not from a tier table
A host that configures a role sees it in the rendered agent file
No new default role-name list is introduced here; that is D3's cell
Any change in a rendered file's shape is named on the cap in terms of what a host sees
